messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (about one‑tenth of atmospheric pressure) pure water freezes at roughly **–2 °C**.  

This comes from the water phase diagram: as pressure drops below the triple point (≈ 611 Pa), the solid–liquid equilibrium line slopes downward, so the melting/freezing temperature falls slightly with decreasing pressure. At 10 kPa the equilibrium temperature is about –2 °C, while the boiling point is around 45 °C.
